title: Cape Breton Home Rebates 2026: Older Houses, Oil Heat and What Is Open
desc: Cape Breton home rebates for 2026: Efficiency Nova Scotia pays up to $5,000, oil-heated homes can add $5,000, HomeWarming is free. Older detached houses in CBRM and what ended.
badge: Up to $5,000, or $10,000 with the income top-up
lead: Cape Breton has some of the oldest housing in Nova Scotia and mostly detached houses that people own. That fits the provincial programs well, because they all pay the homeowner. Here is what is open on October 5, 2026, what ended, and where to start.
cards_heading: What is open for Cape Breton homes in 2026
cards_intro: We re-read the Efficiency Nova Scotia, Government of Nova Scotia and Cape Breton Regional Municipality pages on October 5, 2026. Every amount below comes from those pages.

cards.title: Home Energy Assessment rebates
cards.note: Open to any Nova Scotia homeowner. The $199 assessment comes first, upgrades must be finished within 12 months, and a final visit triggers the cheque.

cards.title: Moderate Income Rebate
cards.note: For owners who live in the home and heat mainly with oil, propane, gas or another non-electric fuel, under the income limits. Wood stoves do not count as a main heat source. Needs approval before work.

cards.title: HomeWarming
cards.note: Insulation, draft-proofing and heat pumps at no charge for lower-income homeowners. Limits are after tax: $30,187 for one person, $57,075 for two to four.

cards.title: Instant rebates at the till
cards.note: Taken off at checkout at participating retailers: $800 for an ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater, $150 for a heat pump dryer, $45 for a smart thermostat for electric heat.

cards.title: Free smart thermostat
cards.note: Professionally installed in electrically heated homes on a residential rate.

cards.title: Heating Assistance Rebate
cards.note: A provincial cheque toward your heating bill. Apply from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.

cards.title: CBRM housing programs
cards.note: The Municipality's grant and tax adjustment are for building new affordable housing such as secondary suites. They do not pay for heat pumps or insulation.

cards.title: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability
cards.note: Closed to new applicants on July 2, 2026.

cards.title: SolarHomes
cards.note: Homeowner applications stopped on April 17, 2025. Only non-profits and charities can still apply.

cards.title: Canada Greener Homes Grant and Loan
cards.note: Both ended: the grant took documents until December 31, 2025, and the loan cannot approve new applications.

sections: Cape Breton's housing, by the numbers

The 2021 Census counted 42,310 households in Cape Breton Regional Municipality. About 68% live in homes built before 1981, compared with 45% in Halifax. Almost three in four (74%) live in single-detached houses and 71% own. Fewer than 1% live in buildings of five or more storeys. The Census also found 9.3% of households in homes that need major repairs.

Owners of detached houses built before 1981 are 45% of all households here, about twice the Halifax share. Those are the households the insulation and heat pump rebates are written for, and the homes most likely to need air sealing first.
Oil heat and the lost federal money

Many older Cape Breton houses were built around an oil furnace, and until July 2, 2026 the federal oil-to-heat-pump program could pay a large share of a switch. It closed when the money ran out, and the province cut its Moderate Income top-up from $10,000 to $5,000. If you were planning around $15,000, plan again. An oil-heated home under the income limits can still get up to $5,000 from the assessment and up to $5,000 from the Moderate Income Rebate, or free work through HomeWarming if income is lower.
Wood heat and the income programs

Efficiency Nova Scotia does not count a wood stove as a primary heating source when it tests for the Moderate Income Rebate. If wood is what heats your house, ask before you apply. HomeWarming asks only that the home is your primary residence and your income is under the limit. Both tests use line 23600 minus line 43500 of your Notice of Assessment.
What the Municipality does and does not offer

Cape Breton Regional Municipality runs housing support programs, but they are aimed at building new affordable rental units, such as a secondary suite or townhouses, and at commercial districts. We found no CBRM rebate or financing program for retrofitting an existing house. Halifax's Solar City financing is for Halifax properties only, so Cape Breton owners paying for solar have no municipal loan option that we could find. The provincial SolarHomes rebate is closed to homeowners.

Cape Breton's average January low is about -6°C, and the coldest reading in the last ten years was -28.2°C. Nova Scotia Power charges the same rate here as elsewhere in the province: 19.128 cents per kWh plus a $20.08 monthly base charge since May 1, 2026. That high rate makes a heat pump water heater and a heat pump worth pricing, and a cold snap is why most homes keep some backup heat.
See our guides for heat pumps, water heaters and insulation in Cape Breton. Ventilators and appliances are covered once for the province: HRV and ventilation rebates and appliance rebates.
claim_heading: What to do first in Cape Breton
claim_steps: Check your after-tax household income against the HomeWarming and Moderate Income limits.
If you qualify, apply first and wait for approval before you book anyone.
Otherwise book a Home Energy Assessment with an Efficiency Nova Scotia delivery partner.
Ask the energy advisor whether insulation and air sealing should come before a heat pump.
Finish within 12 months, then book the final assessment.
If your income is low, apply for the $400 heating rebate before March 31, 2027.
faq: How much can a Cape Breton homeowner get back in 2026?
Up to $5,000 through the Home Energy Assessment program, plus up to $5,000 from the Moderate Income Rebate for homes heated mainly by a non-electric fuel and under the income limits.
Does Cape Breton Regional Municipality have a home energy rebate?
We found none. Its housing programs are for building new affordable housing and for commercial districts.
Is the oil to heat pump program still open?
No. It closed to new applicants on July 2, 2026.
Is there a solar rebate in Cape Breton?
Not for homeowners. SolarHomes closed in April 2025, and Halifax's Solar City financing does not cover Cape Breton.
Do wood-heated homes qualify for the Moderate Income Rebate?
A wood stove is not counted as a primary heating source, so ask Efficiency Nova Scotia how it will treat your home before you apply.
Who can apply for the $400 heating rebate?
People who pay their own heat and have a 2025 net income of $30,000 or less living alone, $45,000 or less with others, or who receive Income Assistance, GIS or the Allowance.
